questions.prompt: Name a Tollywood movie that follows the saviour trope formula.

answers.evidence: Sivudu infiltrates tyrant Bhallaladeva's Mahishmati, frees the captive queen Devasena, and is hailed as the rightful heir 'Baahubali' (Wikipedia plot).
Komaram Bheem, 'the tribe's guardian', travels to Delhi to rescue the Gond girl Malli from the tyrannical British Governor (Wikipedia plot).
Seenu takes up the cause of Neeruru villagers cheated of their land by Aggarwal's corporation and blocks Hyderabad's water supply to force national attention (Wikipedia plot).
Akhanda confronts Varadarajulu's illegal uranium mining, which exploits workers and sickens the region, and protects Murali Krishna's family (Wikipedia plot).
Rishi returns to Ramavaram to save the village from a pipeline project, backing the farmers against businessman Vivek Mittal (Wikipedia plot; IMDb: 'champion for the poor downtrodden farmers').
Sivaji revolts against port don Baji Rao, who exploits refugee labour; the liberated refugees hail him as their saviour and name him 'Chatrapathi' (Wikipedia plot).
Suri liberates the people of Divi from the Odiyappan/Murugan cartel's rule after his brother Siva's death (Wikipedia plot).
Acharya arrives in Dharmasthali to oppose the tyrant Basava's mining plans and protect the villagers and the Gattamma temple (Wikipedia plot).
Hanumanthu gains Hanuman's powers, defeats the tyrant Polygar Gajapathi and protects the people of Anjanadri from Michael (Wikipedia plot).
Narasimha Reddy organises a resistance against East India Company rule that oppressed the villagers (Wikipedia plot).
Ashwatthama and Shambhala's rebels shield SUM-80, mother of the prophesied Kalki, from the totalitarian ruler Supreme Yaskin; Bhairava ends up defending her (Wikipedia plot).
Vedha is the prophesied protector of nine sacred scriptures and must wield the weapon Mirai to defeat Mahabir Lama and save the world (Wikipedia plot).
Nani's Jadal leads the disenfranchised Savaari tribe against the feudal landlord Shikanja Maalik (Wikipedia: 'challenging systemic oppression').

questions.explanation: The 'saviour' formula casts one hero as the protector of a wronged community. Membership is an editorial call made from published plot summaries, not an official genre, so more films qualify than are listed here.
questions.criteria: The hero's central arc is saving or freeing a community, village or people from a tyrant or exploiter (a feudal lord, mining or corporate baron, or colonial power), and the film frames him as their protector. A hero who only fights a personal enemy does not count.
